---
title: "OFS PxWeb / STAT-TAB"
description: "Retrieve a GUI-defined selection, validate wide data, then tidy it."
---

<div class="toolbox-kind">Recipe · verified 2026-10-04</div>

## Workflow

1. Build and understand the selection in STAT-TAB.
2. Open **About table → API Query for this table** and copy the detailed cube URL and query.
3. Retrieve metadata before data.
4. Inspect dimensions, codes, labels and possible aggregate categories.
5. POST the query and preserve the raw JSON-stat2 response.
6. Decode to a dataframe, inspect a wide control table, then create an explicit tidy subset.

The API does not replace the GUI. The verified API roots are language-specific, for example `https://www.pxweb.bfs.admin.ch/api/v1/en` and `/fr`.

## Packages

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(httr2)
library(jsonlite)
library(rjstat)
library(here)

raw_dir <- here("input", "raw")
processed_dir <- here("input", "processed")
```

`rjstat` is the focused dependency used to decode JSON-stat2 into a dataframe.

## Cube URL and metadata

This verified example uses the OFS documentation cube. Replace the URL with the detailed address exported by STAT-TAB.

```r
cube_url <- paste0(
  "https://www.pxweb.bfs.admin.ch/api/v1/en/",
  "px-x-0102030000_101/px-x-0102030000_101.px"
)

metadata_response <- request(cube_url) |>
  req_perform()
resp_check_status(metadata_response)
metadata <- resp_body_json(metadata_response, simplifyVector = FALSE)

metadata$title
```

Flatten every dimension and modality before writing the query:

```r
modalities <- map_dfr(metadata$variables, function(variable) {
  tibble(
    dimension_code = variable$code,
    dimension_label = variable$text,
    value_code = unlist(variable$values),
    value_label = unlist(variable$valueTexts),
    is_time = isTRUE(variable$time),
    can_be_eliminated = isTRUE(variable$elimination)
  )
})

modalities |>
  count(dimension_code, dimension_label, name = "n_modalities")
```

The technical dimension codes may remain German even when `/en` or `/fr` is used. Build queries from `dimension_code` and `value_code`, not translated display labels.

## Flag possible aggregates without deleting them

This diagnostic is intentionally conservative. It reports label candidates for review; it never filters the data.

```r
aggregate_pattern <- regex(
  "(^|\\b)(total|all|overall|ensemble|gesamt|totale)(\\b|$)",
  ignore_case = TRUE
)

aggregate_candidates <- modalities |>
  filter(str_detect(value_label, aggregate_pattern)) |>
  arrange(dimension_code, value_code)

aggregate_candidates
```

Add cube-specific words after inspecting the actual labels. Some aggregates will not match a generic multilingual pattern, and some matching labels may be legitimate categories.

## Dynamic query and raw response

`filter = "top"` with `values = ["3"]` requests the latest three time categories dynamically. `filter = "all"` selects every modality of a dimension.

```r
query <- list(
  query = list(
    list(
      code = "Jahr",
      selection = list(filter = "top", values = list("3"))
    ),
    list(
      code = "Geschlecht",
      selection = list(filter = "all", values = list("*"))
    ),
    list(
      code = "Alter",
      selection = list(filter = "all", values = list("*"))
    )
  ),
  response = list(format = "json-stat2")
)

response <- request(cube_url) |>
  req_body_json(query) |>
  req_perform()
resp_check_status(response)

raw_path <- file.path(raw_dir, "population_age_sex_latest_3_years.json")
dir.create(raw_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
writeBin(resp_body_raw(response), raw_path)
```

The API configuration limits can be inspected at `https://www.pxweb.bfs.admin.ch/api/v1/en/?config`. Keep selections below the current cell limit rather than splitting a request only after it fails.

## Decode and inspect dimensions

```r
raw_json <- readChar(raw_path, file.info(raw_path)$size, useBytes = TRUE)
df_long <- rjstat::fromJSONstat(raw_json) |>
  as_tibble()

glimpse(df_long)
count(df_long, Year)
count(df_long, Sex)
count(df_long, Age)
```

Inspect dimension values rather than trusting only the dataset title. In the verified example, the global JSON-stat label still mentions 2021 while the returned time categories correctly contain 2023–2025.

## Wide first for control

```r
df_wide <- df_long |>
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = Year,
    names_from = c(Sex, Age),
    values_from = value,
    names_sep = " | "
  )

dim(df_wide)
glimpse(df_wide)
```

The wide table makes simultaneously retained totals visible. It is a control representation, not necessarily the best form for later joins or graphics.

## Compare a reported total with components

After inspecting the modalities, name the total and component labels explicitly:

```r
sex_check <- df_long |>
  filter(Age == "Age - total") |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(
    reported_total = value[Sex == "Sex - total"],
    component_sum = sum(value[Sex %in% c("Male", "Female")], na.rm = TRUE),
    difference = reported_total - component_sum,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

sex_check
```

Repeat this logic for every dimension whose totals will coexist with subcategories. A zero difference confirms this particular relationship; it does not authorize summing the total and its components together.

## Create the explicit tidy subset

```r
df_tidy <- df_long |>
  filter(
    Sex %in% c("Male", "Female"),
    Age != "Age - total"
  ) |>
  rename(
    year = Year,
    sex = Sex,
    age = Age,
    population = value
  )

write_csv(
  df_wide,
  file.path(processed_dir, "population_age_sex_control_wide.csv"),
  na = ""
)
write_csv(
  df_tidy,
  file.path(processed_dir, "population_age_sex_tidy.csv"),
  na = ""
)
```

Filtering aggregate categories remains an explicit, cube-specific choice. Never make a helper silently remove labels that merely look like totals.

## Legacy `/sq/` URLs

The earlier `/sq/...` download plus Windows-1252 conversion remains a recovery option for an existing saved query, but it is not the preferred workflow. New work should use the detailed official API URL exported by STAT-TAB and preserve the raw UTF-8 JSON-stat2 response.
